_readme: Per-Actor audit index, built cycle 815 to replace expensive ad hoc grepping through STATUS_ARCHIVE.md/queue_archive.md (see LEARNINGS.md cycle 811 + cycle 814's dead-end search). Fields are the LAST cycle number a given audit type was run, or null if never done / not yet backfilled. Update this file in the SAME cycle you run any of these audit types on an Actor -- add/replace the relevant field with the current cycle number and a one-line note. Keys: varied_test (plain filter-combo rotation), enum_audit (checked enum/vocabulary fields for structurally-dead values), unreachable_remedy (checked that a zero-row message's suggested fix is actually reachable), competitor_audit (compared price/features against the named competitor). Dates below are backfilled from cycles 797-814's own summaries (already read this session, not fresh archaeology) -- treat gaps (nulls) as real unknowns, not omissions. Key added cycle 824: count_audit (checked whether an upstream API's total-match count, when surfaced to buyers, is exhaustive rather than an estimate, and whether deep pages are actually reachable).

app-store-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 833: only one real schema enum, `sort` (mostRecent/mostHelpful/favorable/critical). Unlike every other Actor in the facet-diff rotation, Apple's iTunes RSS review feed (itunes.apple.com/<cc>/rss/customerreviews/id=<id>/sortBy=<X>/page=<N>/json) is directly reachable from this box (no proxy needed, unlike google-news-scraper) -- probed sortBy directly with 13 candidate values incl. the 2 real ones plus 11 plausible-but-unlisted guesses (mostFavorable, mostCritical, topRated, newest, oldest, recent, helpful, rating, relevance, popular, trending). Only mostRecent/mostHelpful (the code's actual 2 API values) returned real entries (50 each); every other candidate returned HTTP 200 with an empty feed (no `entry` key at all) or HTTP 500 -- confirmed by inspecting the raw JSON body, not just entry count. favorable/critical are already correctly documented as client-side re-sorts of mostRecent, not real API params, so the 4-value schema enum is exhaustive and accurate. Clean audit, no code change. NOTE: cycle 832's queue note calling this 'the last enum_audit: null Actor' was wrong -- a fresh count after this cycle shows 12 Actors still null (ats-jobs, eu-ted-tenders, google-play-reviews, nih-reporter, remote-jobs, sam-gov-opportunities, sec-insider-trades, shopify-products, steam-reviews, substack, trademark-search, uk-find-a-tender). The rotation is not done; see queue.md. cycle 845: cycle 843/844 generalization applied here (watch baseline diffed against its own row shape). Apple keeps a review id stable when its author edits their own star rating (feed comment verified live 2026-09-26: a raw RSS entry has only author/rating/title/content/version/votes -- no developer-response field at all, unlike Google Play, so scoreChanged is the only applicable event here, not developerReplied/replyRemoved). Watch baseline was seenIds only -- no rating snapshot -- so an edited review was silently indistinguishable from an unedited one forever. Shipped watchEvents ([new, scoreChanged], empty = both) + watchEvent/previousScore output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (rating 1-5, 0 = pre-845 unknown, never fires) parallel to seenIds. Verified via 5 local round-trip scenarios against real live Apple review data (patching the LOCAL watch KV record, same technique as production KV patches in cycles 843/844, just local so nothing needed cleanup): (1) patched baseline rating differs from live rating + scoreChanged in watchEvents -> fires correctly with correct previousScore, exactly 1 of 20 pushed; (2) same patch + watchEvents:[new] (scoreChanged excluded) -> correctly silent, watchEventsFiltered counted, meta still updated to the live value so it cannot re-fire later; (3) meta silently re-synced after a fire -> third run byte-idempotent (0 pushed); (4) seenMeta key deleted entirely (pre-845 record simulation) -> zero false events, correct predates-change-detection log line; (5) a genuinely-absent id -> delivered as watchEvent:new, previousScore:null. Non-watch default-input regression byte-identical locally AND live on the platform (build 0.1.63, 5/5 charged). check-fail-ordering allowlist line numbers re-verified and updated (907/1146/1162, shifted from 815/1054/1070 by this change -- same 3 guard conditions read live in source, still safe). check-registry-fields/check-code-fields/check-readme-samples all clean after adding watchEvent/previousScore to registry.json output_fields + dataset_schema.json + README (input table, Watch mode section, Use cases bullet, new FAQ entry).

apple-podcasts-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 853: CLEAN NEGATIVE, formally recorded. Cycle 852 guessed this Actor would be the fleet's next counter-field case (rating/review counts, like hacker-news-scraper) -- wrong guess, because watchLabel is explicitly restricted to dataType="episodes" only (src/main.js:103-112); review counts/ratings live under dataType="reviews"/"podcasts", which have no watch mode at all, so the counter-mutation risk never reaches watch-mode code. Checked the episodes watch path itself instead: baseline is a bare id Set (watchId = collectionId:episodeId|episodeGuid|title, main.js:610), no snapshot of any field. But the README (line 40, "Watch mode" section) promises ONLY new-episode detection ("only episodes not delivered under that label before") -- unlike every other watch-mode Actor in the fleet (Shopify/Play/App Store/Steam/ATS/court-records/HN), it never promises a field-change alert on an already-delivered id, so the watch-subset-shape defect (a promised field-change silently missed because the baseline is narrower than the row) cannot apply here by definition -- there is no promised change signal to miss. Checked the plausible mutation candidates anyway (explicit-tag correction, duration correction, releaseDate correction under a stable episodeId) and confirmed episodePassesFilters() runs BEFORE the watchSeen check (main.js:607-616), so an episode that initially fails a filter (e.g. explicitFilter=clean excluding a mistagged-explicit episode) is never added to the baseline and self-heals if corrected later -- same accidental-coverage shape Play had (cycle 844). No code change.

ats-jobs-scraper.note: cycle 817: provider-by-provider live reachability pass, all 7 ATSes (greenhouse/ashby/lever/recruitee/workable/smartrecruiters/workday) hit directly against their real default-company boards. All 200s, all field shapes match code expectations exactly. No structural drift, no bugs. cycle 818: competitor_audit via apify-admin store 'ats jobs scraper'/'greenhouse jobs' -- real leader by user count is automation-lab/multi-ats-jobs-scraper (161 users, FREE tier $0.00115/job + $0.005 one-time start) and webdata_labs/greenhouse-lever-ashby-jobs-scraper (65 users, $0.001/job flat, no start fee, only 4 platforms vs our 7). Our FREE tier was $0.0015/job, 30-50% above both. Feature-wise we already lead on breadth (7 ATS platforms vs their 4-5), so no feature gap -- price was the real gap. Cut FREE tier $0.0015->$0.001 (matches webdata_labs, ~13% below automation-lab), scaled BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD+ tiers proportionally (0.00085/0.00075/0.0007), still ~7x over the ~$0.0001/item HTTP-only compute floor. Verified live via API pull post-publish, check-pricing 0 drift, check-charges 24/24 clean. | cycle 847 watch-subset-shape pass (h843-846 technique, same class as shopify/play/app-store/steam): watch baseline was jobId-only, no salary snapshot. Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever/Recruitee postings commonly publish without a salary and add one later under the same jobId (pay-transparency add-on or a plain edit) -- SmartRecruiters/Workable/Workday never carry a salary at all (confirmed in their own mappers), so salaryAdded simply never fires for those. Shipped watchEvents ([new, salaryAdded], empty=both) + watchEvent/previousHasSalary output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (1=hasSalary,2=noSalary,0=unknown/pre-847, never fires) parallel to seenIds, mirroring the chargeAndPush-bypasses-the-seen-guard shape steam-reviews-scraper (h846) needed. Verified via 5 local round-trips (real Greenhouse airbnb baseline; a patched no-salary->has-salary flip fires salaryAdded with correct previousHasSalary/salaryMin/salaryMax; watchEvents:[new] excludes it but still resyncs meta so it cannot spuriously re-fire; idempotent re-run; seenMeta-deleted pre-847 baseline -> 0 false events + correct warm-up log line) AND live: default-input regression (build 0.1.50) SUCCEEDED, 52/52 rows byte-identical shape to before, chargedEventCounts {job:50}; a real watch baseline on ashby:ramp + a production-KV-store patch via the API on a real posting -> salaryAdded fired correctly, chargedEventCounts {job:1}, previousHasSalary:false matching the patch and the real live salaryMin/Max on the row. Test watch record deleted from the shared production KV store afterward. Also confirmed substack-scraper has NO watch mode at all (no watchEvents/seenIds/WATCH_KV anywhere in its source) -- the queue note carrying it forward as the next watch-subset-shape candidate since cycle 845 was simply wrong; removed from the rotation. | cycle 887 varied_test: combo 1 (departmentKeyword="Engineering" across all 7 ATS default companies) came back clean -- only greenhouse/ashby/leverdemo contributed rows but department field IS populated (not missing) for recruitee/workable/smartrecruiters/workday, they genuinely have no Engineering-named department in the sample, not a bug. Combo 2 (locationKeyword="United States", the exact phrase the README/schema use as their own worked example) found and FIXED a real cross-ATS bug: Lever sends raw country="US"/"GB"/"CA", SmartRecruiters sends lowercase "us", Recruitee sends the Dutch locale name "Nederland" -- none contain "united states" as a substring, so searching the documented example silently returned 0/13 real US rows from Lever+SmartRecruiters (live-verified leverdemo 0/10, ElasticBandCompany 0/2) with no warning, while greenhouse/ashby/workday (which already emit full English country names) passed fine and made the bug invisible without a per-ATS category breakdown. Shipped normalizeCountry() (build 0.1.51): a small code-to-name alias map applied to the 3 affected mappers -- correct at the data-quality root (the country OUTPUT field itself, not just the filter), unlike the cycle-784 Greenhouse employmentType case which had no fix and could only be disclosed. Live-verified post-fix: same locationKeyword="United States" query on lever+smartrecruiters -> 11/11 rows (9 lever + 2 smartrecruiters), all correctly showing country:"United States". Default-input regression clean (32/32 rows, all 7 ATS present, country values now consistently English: United States/United Kingdom/Netherlands). check-charges/check-pricing/check-code-fields all 0 drift.

clinicaltrials-scraper.note: cycle 816: all 6 exposed vocabularies checked live registry-wide (14 overallStatus, 3 studyTypes, 6 phases, 3 ageGroups, 3 documentTypes, resultsAvailability, sex) -- every value real and non-empty, nothing to remove. Two stale schema descriptions fixed instead (fdaRegulationViolation 'a few dozen' -> 8; phases '~19% no phase' -> 23.7% + corrected the device-trial parenthetical). Build 0.1.32, both claims re-verified by platform run. cycle 822: rowsPerStudy's 'averages 5 sites (max seen: 110)' claim (flagged as never-checked by cycle 821's sweep) was live-verified via a 5000-study sample of CT.gov v2 -- badly wrong. Real distribution is heavily skewed: median 1 site, mean ~6 (close to the old '5'), but max is 1,089 (not 110) and 49/5000 (~1%) studies have >100 sites. The 110 max understated the real row-multiplier ceiling for site mode by ~10x. Fixed the schema description with the real mean/median/max and reframed the multiplier as 1x-1000x+ depending on trial size rather than a flat ~5x. Shipped build 0.1.33, read back live from the API to confirm. Also live-checked nih-reporter-scraper's '~3% no award_amount' FY2024 claim via a 10,000-project live sample: 2.66% (95% CI ~2.3-3.0%) -- holds up, no fix needed. cycle 837: fleet-wide grep for cycle 836 TED defect-3 shape (unconditional "re-run in a few minutes" advice on a watch-baseline seed failure, regardless of whether apiGet failed via an immediate 4xx or a genuinely exhausted 429/5xx/network retry loop). Found the SAME bug on 3 Actors sharing this apiGet/seedBaseline pattern. Root cause: apiGet returns null for both an immediate non-200 (bad input, no retry) and a retry-exhausted 429/5xx/network fault, and the caller collapsed both into one failure state with one unconditional message. Fix: capture the HTTP status at the point of failure (lastErrorStatus / w.lastErrorStatus / incompleteStatus, default-evaluated at call time so a later successful call cant clobber it) and branch the final Actor.fail()/log.warning message on INPUT_ERROR_STATUS={400,404,422} vs transient. Verified for each Actor with a REAL upstream 400 reachable through an unvalidated free-text field the code passes straight through (federal-register-scraper: cfrPart="zzz-bogus-part" -> real 400; court-records-scraper: query="(unbalanced" Lucene syntax -> real 400; clinicaltrials-scraper: searchQuery="(unbalanced" Essie syntax -> real 400) -- each now correctly says the API is rejecting the input and not to blindly retry. Also re-verified a normal valid input still succeeds on all 3 (regression, local + one live platform run each on federal-register-scraper). Builds: federal-register-scraper 0.1.25, court-records-scraper 0.1.31, clinicaltrials-scraper 0.1.34.

Added a `watchChangeBlindFilters` computation right after the watch-init block (main.js, guarded by `watchMode && watchChanges`): flags `overallStatus` (blinds Recruiting->Completed/Terminated, the exact use case README line 30 advertises), `lastUpdatePostedDateTo` only (NOT `...From` -- an update only ever moves lastUpdatePostDate LATER, so a lower bound can never be defeated by the change being watched for), and `primaryCompletionDateFrom`/`To` + `studyCompletionDateFrom`/`To` (either bound, since a completion-date revision can move either direction). Two split log.warning lines (what's wrong / what to do) to avoid the platform's `[line-too-long]` truncation cycle 860 hit; `watchChangeBlindFilters` added to RUN_SUMMARY (null outside watchChanges, [] when clean); README gained a matching FAQ pair ("don't filter on the field you're watching" + "what to do") and a RUN_SUMMARY sample/prose update. Verified live on build 0.1.35: a seed run with `overallStatus:['RECRUITING']` + `watchChanges:true` produced exactly 1 untruncated blind-filter entry + 2 full warning lines (confirmed via `grep -ci line-too-long` on the run log = 0) and RUN_SUMMARY.watchChangeBlindFilters populated; an otherwise-identical seed with no status filter produced RUN_SUMMARY.watchChangeBlindFilters:[] and no warning; the Actor's own exampleRunInput (non-watch) SUCCEEDED 12/12 charged with no _watch* leakage, confirming no regression on the ordinary path. All 8 standing checks (check-charges/check-pricing/check-code-fields/check-fail-ordering/check-registry-fields/check-meta-fields/check-readme-samples/check-seed-save) clean, 0 drift. Both test KV baselines deleted from `fetchsmith-clinicaltrials-watch`. **This closes the change-blind-filter class fleet-wide (both instances found by the cycle-860/861 sweep are now fixed) -- next cycle should pick a genuinely new defect class rather than extending this sweep.**

This closes the fleet's FEC pagination/timeout work opened across cycles 855/856/857; no further pagination follow-up queued for this Actor. cycle 856 (superseded detail below): FIX SHIPPED (build 0.1.31 / source 0.1.7). Closed queue item 0-TODO-h855-pagination. ROOT CAUSE, reproduced live before touching code: Postgres sorts NULLs FIRST on a DESC sort, and schedule_a/schedule_b were queried with sort=-contribution_receipt_date / -disbursement_date and NO sort_nulls_last (schedule_e has always had sort_nulls_last:'true' -- A and B were the odd ones out). A real minority of Schedule A/B rows have a NULL date (F3X filers leave the itemization date blank), so any match set containing one starts with a block of dateless rows, and inside that block FEC's keyset cursor is {last_index, sort_null_only:true} with NO last_<date> value. The code explicitly stripped sort_null_only from the cursor ('a flag, not a cursor value'), so page 2 carried last_index alone -> HTTP 422 'both values from the previous page's last_indexes object are needed'. Verified: unfiltered 2026 schedule_a page 1 = 100 rows, ALL dates null, li={last_index, sort_null_only:true}; replaying page 2 with last_index only = 422 (the exact cycle-855 error), with sort_null_only=true = 200. KEY FINDING -- forwarding sort_null_only ALONE IS NOT A FIX, it converts a loud failure into SILENT TRUNCATION: on a deliberately mixed 2-committee match set (C00406892 = 320 dateless rows, C00002469 = 13,693 dated rows) the sort_null_only walk delivered all 320 dateless rows then returned last_indexes={} at page 5 -- i.e. 'exhausted' -- never reaching ANY of the 13,693 dated rows. A PPE buyer would be charged for 320 useless rows and told that was the whole result set. FIX = both halves: (1) primary -- sort_nulls_last:'true' added to schedule_a and schedule_b (parity with schedule_e), so dateless rows go to the TAIL and the useful walk always carries a real date cursor; (2) defensive -- stop stripping sort_null_only (normalised to the string 'true', false/null dropped) so the trailing null block pages instead of 422ing. VERIFIED on platform build 0.1.31: same mixed-set walk with sort_nulls_last started at the newest dated rows and paged 8+ pages on a proper date cursor; a real filtered run (donorEmployer BOEING, electionYear 2026, maxResults 45) SUCCEEDED across 3 pages -- 45 rows, 0 nulls, dates verified strictly descending 2026-08-31 -> 2026-08-27, so the page-2/3 cursors genuinely work; default-input gate (candidateName Warren) SUCCEEDED, 3 results, no regression. All 8 standing checks clean, 0 drift. NEW BEHAVIOUR / NOT A REGRESSION BUT WORTH KNOWING: sort_nulls_last makes the fully UNFILTERED contributions scan (electionYear only, ~173M matching rows) too expensive upstream -- it 504s on curl and now times out fecGet's 30s request budget on page 1, so that one shape fails with 0 rows charged instead of failing with 100 dateless rows charged. Judged net-positive and shipped; the unactionable timeout message is queued as 0-TODO-h856-unfiltered. The trailing-null-block transition (half 2) is defensive and NOT live-verified -- reaching it needs all dated rows exhausted first (137+ pages on the smallest mixed set found), so it was out of budget to prove.

hacker-news-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 852: GAP CLOSED and shipped (build 0.1.47, source 0.1.5, commit dedf48d) -- 7th instance of the watch-subset-shape defect, and the first one that needed a different mechanism rather than a port of the fleet's diff-and-fire pattern. watchSeen is now a Map of `{p: points, c: numComments}` snapshots, and the new `watchChanges` input re-delivers an already-seen item ONLY when a count crosses a rung of a tunable milestone ladder (`watchPointMilestones` default 25/50/100/250/500/1000/2500/5000, `watchCommentMilestones` default 25/50/100/250/500/1000; either blank disables that signal) that the previous snapshot had not yet reached. Each rung pays out at most once per item because the snapshot advances on EVERY sight, delivered or not: measured in the local test, a story climbing 51->99 points one point per run fires 0 times and a whole 0->3000-point life costs 7 extra rows, not 3000 -- which is what makes a counter field safe to watch at all. Unknown-baseline marker is PRESENCE of the `p` key, not a null value (`p: null` is the real snapshot of a comment hit, since Algolia attaches no points to comments) -- same trap court-records-scraper hit with `dateTerminated: null`. Pre-0.1.5 flat-string-id baselines decode to the no-snapshot marker and resync on first re-sight, so existing watches keep working and never fire against a backlog they never captured. Snapshot is only advanced on an actual delivery when PPE charging succeeds, so a charge cap defers a milestone instead of silently consuming it. Outputs `_watchChangeType`/`_watchPrevious`/`_watchMilestone`; `watchChangedCount` reported separately from `watchNewCount` in RUN_SUMMARY and the webhook. Verified: 11-case local logic test (no re-fire on a climb, highest-rung-only on a 10->600 jump, silent on a falling score, silent on an unknown baseline, silent sitting on a cleared rung, empty ladders disable), live platform seed + incremental round-trip (KV record holds `{i,p,c}` objects, 279 ids, 0 charged both runs), clean default-input gate with no `_watch*` leakage into non-watch rows.

Build 0.1.43. cycle 846 watch-subset-shape pass (h843/844/845's technique, same class as shopify/play/app-store): watch baseline was `seenIds` only, no `voted_up` snapshot. Steam keeps recommendationid stable when an author edits their own review in place (verified live: real reviews on appId 570 with timestamp_updated well after timestamp_created, same recommendationid both times) -- exactly how a player flips their own thumbs-up/thumbs-down, so an already-delivered review's flip was invisible to a watch forever. Steam reviews have no developer-response feature at all, so only one new event applies (unlike Play). Shipped `watchEvents` (`new`/`recommendationChanged`, empty=both) + `watchEvent`/`previousRecommended`, backed by a `seenMeta` array parallel to `seenIds` (1=true,2=false,0=unknown/pre-846, never fires). First implementation attempt had a real bug caught by live round-trip testing: `pushResult`'s own already-in-watchSeen guard unconditionally skipped the recommendationChanged case too (that id IS in watchSeen on purpose) -- fixed by splitting out a `chargeAndPush` helper with no such guard, called directly by the changed-branch, same shape app-store-reviews-scraper already used. Verified via 5 local round-trips (change fires correctly with right previousRecommended; watchEvents:['new'] excludes it but still resyncs so it can't spuriously re-fire; idempotent re-run; seenMeta-deleted pre-846 baseline -> 0 false events + correct warm-up log line; genuinely-new id -> delivered as watchEvent:'new') AND live on the platform: default-input regression SUCCEEDED (10/10 charged, byte-identical shape), then a real watch baseline + a production-KV-store patch via the API on a real review id -> recommendationChanged fired correctly, chargedEventCounts {result:1}, previousRecommended:false/recommended:true matched the patch. Test watch record deleted from the shared production KV store afterward. Build 0.1.44.

trademark-search-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 858: GAP CLOSED and shipped (Apify build 0.1.17, source 0.1.1). Watch mode was id-only (st13), so a mark whose status moved Pending/Filed->Registered->Opposed/Expired on an already-delivered id was invisible forever -- flagged as a known, deliberately out-of-scope gap in the code comment since watch mode first shipped ("tracking that transition needs re-querying every known id, out of scope for this pass"). Shipped watchChanges (default false, so existing watches are unaffected): watchSeen is now a Map id->{status} snapshot; a status move on an already-seen mark is re-delivered tagged _watchChangeType:["status"]/_watchPrevious:{status}, billed at the normal per-row price; an unchanged mark is silently skipped and its snapshot kept current so turning watchChanges on later only detects drift from that point, not a backlog. Legacy flat-array baselines (pre-this-cycle) load with a null snapshot per id, so their first post-upgrade sighting cannot be a false-positive change (same rule as grants-gov-scraper). Verified live end-to-end, not just locally: seeded a real 8-mark baseline (searchTerm solarwinds, office EM, niceClasses 9+42), fetched the persisted KV record via the API and confirmed the compact {i,s} shape, overwrote 2 of the 8 entries with fabricated prior statuses via a direct PUT, reran incrementally with watchChanges:true -- exactly those 2 marks (and only those 2) came back tagged with the correct _watchChangeType/_watchPrevious matching the fabricated values, the other 6 were skipped and not charged (log line: "0 new mark(s) and 2 changed mark(s) (status)"). Test KV records deleted from the shared production store afterward. All 8 standing checks clean, 0 drift. README/input_schema/package.json updated.

uk-find-a-tender-scraper.note: cycle 838: enum_audit — stages exclusion-probe on both FTS and Contracts Finder. FTS silently returns 0 for any stage outside {planning,tender,award}, no error, even though its own data has contract/implementation/*Update/*Cancellation/*Amendment tags. CF validates server-side (400 "X is not a valid OCDS stage") and genuinely accepts 5: planning/tender/award/contract/implementation, all with real non-trivial data. us-federal-awards-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 859: CLEAN NEGATIVE, no code change. us-federal-awards-scraper.varied_test_note: cycle 884: REAL BUG FOUND, fixed + shipped (build 0.1.41). Two clean multi-filter combos first: (1) agencies=[Department of Veterans Affairs]+placeOfPerformanceStates=[TX]+naicsCodes=[5415]+minAwardAmount=1000000+startDate/endDate 2023-2024 -> 10/10 rows satisfied agency+state+NAICS-prefix+amount simultaneously (rows' own startDate falling outside the window is the already-documented coarse time_period behaviour, README FAQ line ~172, not a bug). (2) awardCategories=[contracts,idvs]+pscCodes=[R4]+recipientStates=[CA]+min/maxAwardAmount 500k-50M+expiringWithinDays=365+includeOpportunityScore -> 10/10 rows satisfied all six constraints. BUT every row was awardCategory=contracts, and probing the idvs half alone returned 0 rows; dropping expiringWithinDays made the same idvs query return rows with endDate=null. Root cause: USAspending reports NO period-of-performance end date for IDVs (live-verified 10/10 broad-sample IDVs, 4+ agencies, start years 2008-2025, all endDate null), so the client-side passesExpiringFilter dropped 100% of IDVs SILENTLY -- while input_schema advertised the filter as a recompete radar for 'contracts/grants/IDVs' and claimed the only exclusions (subaward, loans) were 'dropped with a warning, not silently charged'. Only the subaward warning was actually implemented; loans were silently dropped too. Fix: added NO_END_DATE_CATEGORIES={idvs,loans} startup warning naming the blind categories, and saying either 'Only [<usable>] can match this run' or, when every selected category is blind, that the run will return zero rows plus which categories to use instead. Corrected the false IDV claim in input_schema description, the zero-row hint message, and 4 README spots (lines 13/40/182). Verified live on platform: blind-only run logs the zero-row warning, mixed contracts+idvs run logs 'Only [contracts] can match this run' and still returns the identical 5 correct rows (no regression). Grants confirmed to carry real endDates so the corrected docs introduce no new false claim.
